entry_points.text: Eventfd control checks flags against deassign bit and identifier against mask, assigning with descriptor or deassigning by identifier with existence and absence errors; Hyper-V lock serializes alloc and removal, removal waits grace before releasing the event, and user copy failure reports fault.

GSI mapping walks routing under read-side protection with fallback when table or entry missing; IRQ setting maps the line, invokes chip handlers, sums successes and fails when none accepts, serving legacy and modern controllers without probing.

exports.text: Hypercall needs supervisor privilege and protected mode via PE test else undefined-opcode and stop; it decodes opcode, headers, fast flag, repeat fields with derived repeat flag and guest addresses with trace, enforces cached-enlightenment policy with mask, debug and extended-call rules unless disabled, allows vector fast input only for flush variants and extended IPI with FPU capture into descriptor slots, validates per-code repeat/header/fast combos, then completes inline, yields, flushes, forwards message/event/debug/extended to userspace exit with control and addresses plus completion, or rejects with invalid, denied or operation-denied statuses.

VM init prepares Hyper-V lock and connection table; CPUID fills fixed ordered vendor, interface, version, feature, enlightenment, limit, debug and nested leaves from vCPU, nested and topology state, failing too-big when caller count is short and clamping when long, with limits, nested version/flush/perf, debug vendor/interface/capability values fixed and unlisted leaves unchanged.

Create allocates PIT, initializes mutex, timer, worker and ack state, resets channels, enables reinject and registers timer and speaker ports with unwind; free holds slots lock around unregister, disables reinject, cancels timer, destroys worker and frees, doing nothing when absent.

Bus registration needs slots lock, inserts ranges sorted via copy-on-write with ordered publish and grace reclaim, rejecting at limit or allocation failure; PIC offers pin injection with out-of-range sentinel, output refresh, acknowledge clearing global output first and returning a vector, and mask broadcast resolving chip-pin to global with notification only for matches under read guard.

hazards.text: Service clearing drops the PIC spinlock around external callbacks allowing interleaved arrivals, with deferred wakeup after unlock kicking the first capable vCPU.

invariants.text: Hypercall is enabled only with arch flag and guest OS identifier, disabled builds report false and deny; auto end-of-interrupt follows the per-vector bitmap when per-vCPU state exists else false; nested flush reads cached nested flags.

Spin marks in-spin with yield eligibility as a pair, best-effort yields round-robin after last boosted skipping caller and unsuitable and recording target, then clears marks; alt builds make marks no-ops; targets must be ready, satisfy blocking, kernel preemption with interrupt policy and eligibility toggling in-spin with relaxation intercept; runnable means arch-runnable or async-fault pending, arch-runnable means running without halt, unhalt or events; in-kernel treats protected guests as in-kernel else compares privilege with weak defaults; selection is racy and approximate.

Pending events disjoin async-fault completions, allowed init/SIPI, queued exceptions with triple fault, NMI/SMI/PMI subject to allowance, protected-guest updates, allowed maskable interrupts, synthetic timers, nested guest-mode and Xen events; interrupt presence checks external first, then protected-guest helper, else LAPIC, folding kernel/user LAPIC, Xen upcall, PIC acceptance from LAPIC enable, LVT masking and delivery, and kernel IOAPIC versus split userspace vector.

Requests test and clear atomically with barrier and masked index, forbidding dead-VM at compile time; assist passes when state absent or page disabled else fetches; nested transitions re-raise flush with paging assist for per-level recheck; timing and init are no-ops; purge consumes request then discards with disabled variant idle, forming request, per-level queue and purge on entry or level change.

Timer accesses validate range and mask to channel, index three is control on write and empty success on read; count writes use low, high or two-part word order; reads prefer status over latched count over live counter with staged consumption; live single-byte reads stay stable while word reads alternate; speaker stores data from bit one and channel-two gate from bit zero, reads combine data, gate, output and refresh toggle; reset forces terminal mode, gates except channel two, reloads zero and resets reinject; extended restore starts only on rising legacy entry for channel zero; state get/set with reinject run locked with reload; creation converts count to interval with host-minimum clamp and absolute start; writes decode read-back versus counter-select; unmask resets reinject; out-of-range is rejected and reads truncate.

Ranges order by start then end with zero-length as exact match; pin level ORs source bits; level pins track request with level, edge pins set request only on rising history; masked injection returns negative else reports change; priority scans from offset with empty sentinel; pending masks by inverted mask, hides slave cascade under special nested master and signals only when outranking service; slave pulses master cascade first; acknowledge sets service, clears edge requests, handles auto end-of-interrupt with rotation and fallback vectors; reset preserves level requests and clears edge, mask, offset, special, selector and init while conditionally clearing nested, auto and service; pins below eight select master.

locks.text: Yield try-locks the identifier, references the task when present, unlocks, yields, then drops the reference; missing lock, identifier or task means no yield.
PIT mutex guards channel, flag, port and ioctl paths with loaders asserting hold; migration pins ownership to the boot vCPU with mutex held around timer restart.

PIC spinlock uses paired helpers; interrupt mutex guards ack and mask notifier updates with removal synchronizing; reinject toggling avoids redundant work, inhibits APIC acceleration while armed, manages notifiers, preserves state and requests IOAPIC rescan when in kernel.

state_machines.text: Modes zero to five form terminal, retriggerable and periodic families; gate edges reload retriggerable and periodic members, expiry wraps to top, loads arm per family with zero mapping to full range; elapsed uses remaining time for timer channel and timestamps otherwise, scaling by frequency with per-mode wrap and level rules and HPET legacy handling; square odd counts and strobe are approximate with null-count unimplemented.

Count and status latches hold until consumed; timer bumps pending when reinject armed, queues worker and restarts periodic else stops; reset clears pending and marks acked; ack orders before pending check and re-queues when ticks remain; worker skips when reinject armed but unacked else pulses PIT line and fans watchdog NMI in virtual-wire mode; absent state safely skips.

Writes decode low address bit for command versus data; data walks init base through intermediate to mode then masks, command splits init, operation control and end-of-interrupt; end-of-interrupt clears highest service with optional offset advance and refresh except plain rotation; operation control sets poll, read selection and special mask; mask updates emit per-pin notices before refresh; output latches wakeup only on rising edge.

structs.text: Synthetic timer holds hrtimer, index, config, count, expiry, pending message and delivery flag; synthetic controller holds version, control, message and event pages, per-entry routing, 256-bit auto end-of-interrupt and presence bitmaps plus active and preservation flags.

Each flush queue pairs a write spinlock for cross-vCPU producers with a guest-physical FIFO, one per nested level with enumeration count; per-vCPU Hyper-V state links owner, records index, APIC address and runtime offset, embeds controller, exit buffers, timers, pending bitmap and CPUID flag, caches feature and nested leaves, holds scratch banks and masks, assist copy and nested page and identity values.

Channel holds full and latched counts with presence, status, read and write sequencers, latches, transfer and operating modes, BCD, gate and timestamp; PIT state holds three channels with flags, periodic marker, period and timer then mutex, reinject, pending and ack counters and notifier with earlier fields under mutex; PIT object holds devices, VM pointer, state, notifier, worker and expired work.

Flush depth is 16 with all-bits-set full-flush sentinel; signature is 0x31237648 with debug leaves 0x40000080, 81 and 82; kernel-debug uses BIT 1 and hypercall transport BIT 2; debug control, status, send, receive, pending and options are 0x400000F1, F2, F3, F4, F5 and FF.
Access modes are 1 low, 2 high, 3 word-low and 4 word-high; timer base 64, speaker 97, timer length 4, frequency 1193181, channel mask low two bits, and maximum interval tick rate divided by 100.
